5. I rewrote Research_Visit.md following the narrative structure — removing all technical details, focusing on research narrative.

6. The user then provided the exact slide-by-slide content (12 slides) to paste. I reformatted the document to match this exact slide structure.

8. I rewrote again with specific content: actual statistics (424 stations, 10 years, 45% hydropower, 8 experiments, MESAN, SMHI), specific findings (gradient balance mechanism, task reframing from detection to forecasting, MLP vs LSTM finding), real timelines.

9. The user then asked to create a poster-like SVG visualization of Research_Visit.md — but then immediately followed with a /compact command asking for a summary of recent messages. So the SVG task was interrupted by the compact command.

User rejected this approach with detailed guidance: "If a slide answers WHAT you coded, remove it. If a slide answers WHY the visit mattered, keep it."
